synopsis: Every executed virtual test should be reproducible from an immutable provenance manifest identifying requirements and hazards, scenario versions and parameters, machine and sensor configurations, software and model versions, random seeds, raw-data checksums, metrics and verdicts; failed validation cases must also remain in the record [f7104, f7108, f7109, f7590]. Reproducibility extends to captured-site dates, coordinates and revision histories, and to archiving toolchain versions, binaries or containers, drivers and assets; neutral formats and canonical data outside vendor formats help avoid costly supplier dependence [f4376, f9386, f7116, f8876, f8886]. Large synchronized camera, lidar and radar programmes create storage, retention, privacy, access-control and provenance obligations, but the research did not establish recording data rates, storage sizes, logger requirements or jurisdiction-specific governance requirements, so these questions need early resolution [f5799, f5800, f5801, f5803]. Evidence may be disclosed in litigation, and the booklet identifies record-keeping and liability from 9 December 2026 as planning blind spots; early legal review, explicit retention policies and preservation of raw evidence, model versions and sign-offs are recommended [f9804, f10362, f10848, f11061, f10706]. Storage and retention also affect throughput and recurring cost: cost figures were not found, and an end-to-end benchmark should measure cost, wall time, storage and analyst hours to identify whether compute, storage or human triage becomes the bottleneck [f10745, f10791, f10957, f10958].
